title: How do bees see ultraviolet light?
examples: Why do flowers have patterns we can't see?

figure.name: x-compare
figure.verdict: Bees see hidden UV signs that point the way to nectar

explain.say: We see colour using three kinds of cone cell, tuned to red, green and blue. Honeybees also have three kinds, but theirs are tuned to ultraviolet, blue and green.

explain.say: So bees can see ultraviolet light, which is invisible to us, but they cannot see red. A red flower looks dark to a bee unless it also reflects ultraviolet.

explain.say: Many flowers have ultraviolet patterns, like bullseyes and stripes, called nectar guides. They lead the bee to the nectar, and the bee carries pollen as it goes.

explain.say: Each bee eye is made of thousands of tiny units with their own lenses. Bees see less detail than we do, but they spot movement and flickering petals quickly.

faq.a: Yes. One of a honeybee's three colour receptors is tuned to ultraviolet light, so bees see patterns on flowers that are invisible to us. They cannot see red, which we can.
Not really. Bees lack a red receptor, so pure red looks dark or black to them. Poppies look red to us, but bees see them because they reflect ultraviolet.

What colour does red look to a bee?

faq.a: Nectar guides are patterns on petals, often visible only in ultraviolet, that point towards the centre of the flower like a runway, guiding bees to the nectar and pollen.
asks: Why do flowers have patterns we can't see?

faq.a: A compound eye is made of thousands of tiny units called ommatidia, each with its own lens, pointing in slightly different directions. Together they build a mosaic picture of the world.
asks: How many lenses does a bee eye have?

faq.q: How do scientists know what bees see?
faq.a: Researchers trained bees to find sugar water at certain colours, then tested which colours they could tell apart. Karl von Frisch did famous experiments like this in the early 1900s.

facts: Honeybees have photoreceptors sensitive to ultraviolet, blue and green light, but none for red.
Many flowers have ultraviolet patterns called nectar guides that are invisible to human eyes.

quiz.say: Which colour can a bee see that a human cannot?
quiz.why: Bees have an ultraviolet receptor, so they see UV patterns on flowers.

wrong.1: Red is the colour bees cannot see well.
wrong.2: Infrared is detected by pit vipers, not bees.
